draft.title: Revising for clarity and coherence
card: Revising means looking again at a draft to make it better. It is different from proofreading, which fixes spelling and punctuation.
Order
check that ideas follow a logical order. If a point seems to jump in from nowhere, move it to where it fits.
Links
check that paragraphs link. Linking words and phrases such as "however", "as a result" and "in the same way" show how one idea connects to the next.
Clarity
check that each sentence says exactly what is meant. Cut extra words, swap vague words such as "stuff" for exact ones, and fix sentences that could be read two ways.
draft.remember: Revise by checking order, links between paragraphs, and exact meaning.

a.q: Which action is revising for coherence, not just proofreading?
opts: Moving a paragraph so the ideas follow a logical order
Correcting a misspelt word in the second paragraph
Adding a missing full stop at the end of a sentence
Changing a lower case letter to a capital after a full stop
a.why: Coherence is about how ideas fit together, so moving a paragraph into a logical order is revising. The other three fix spelling or punctuation, which is proofreading.
a.clue: Which change affects how the ideas connect, not the spelling?

b.q: Leo's draft has three short sentences. The first says the school needs more bins. The second says litter is everywhere. The third adds that the canteen sells many snacks. Which revision makes his writing clearer?
opts: Our school needs more bins because litter covers the yard
Our school needs more bins and stuff for the yard area
Our school needs bins. Litter. The canteen sells snacks
Our school needs more bins, and bins are needed here too
b.why: The first option links the need to its reason with "because" and uses exact words. The second swaps in a vague word, "stuff". The third is choppy and has no links. The fourth only repeats itself.
b.clue: Look for the option that links the ideas and uses exact words.

a.best: Moving a paragraph so the ideas follow a logical order

b.best: Our school needs more bins because litter covers the yard

problems.detail: Why (b) names options by position ('The first option… The second… The third… The fourth'), but the options are shuffled. In the order shown, the 'stuff' option comes first and the 'because' option comes third, so the why describes the wrong options.

The stem mentions a third sentence about the canteen selling snacks, but the right option simply drops it. The card says to move a point that 'jumps in from nowhere' to where it fits, not to delete it, so students may be unsure how the canteen idea is meant to be handled.
